dust.text:
The bells arrive over the water before the animals do. A salt caravan has come down to the shingle while the boat waits out the afternoon: six donkeys, a boy running ahead to clear the path, and a master who looks at your face, then at the empty skin at your belt, and says nothing about either. He lifts a hand, and the line stops.

"You are ashore dry," he says. "That is a choice, or it is bad planning. Which?"

choices.text: Drink, and give thanks to whatever brought them.
Ask for a place in the shade until the heat passes.

provenance.notes: Travelers sharing water is a plausible road custom; the scene is invented.
